frontMatter.title: Phase 06 evidence: desktop SDK, CLI and terminal effects (execution support matrix)

summary: Phase 06 put managed admission at the actual process sinks on feature/mega-maestro-v1.1.0-rc in the Maestro checkout (macOS, Darwin 27, Node v26.12.0): the desktop process manager admits every spawn before any branch against a live host authority port and binds a lease to the process for its lifetime; the child spawner confines the admitted launch at startTurn's gate and the PTY, SSH, OpenCode-server and one-off shell routes refuse explicitly as unavailable; the Codex app-server and OpenCode sinks decide each tool effect from a live effect authority bound to lease, thread, turn and request and never fall back to an unrestricted path; the bare CLI reads the managed binding and refuses on an enrolled machine while a host-injected authority admits every spawn afresh; terminal input reaches only admitted processes; and the permission relay decides managed-first, intersected with user consent. The desktop's effect authority is unavailable in this build because the endpoint socket exposes no per-effect operation, so on a managed desktop every real provider route is refused or declined today, explicitly, and nothing counts as a positive real-provider result. Verified locally with deterministic tests over the real lease authority and declared doubles; the real pair remains blocked on the same Mega-Maestro producers as phases 04 and 05.
lineBudgetNotes: MRC-06-01 (710) is over the 500-line guideline: its three named files hold the sink (ProcessManager +330, types +95, the two handlers +80) and the overage is the new 113-line desktop port, the service and startup wiring (06-01A) and the handler test mock that the first run showed needed the admitted spawn (06-01B), all in the same commit. MRC-06-05 (523, of which 155 removed) replaced three hand-copied lease gates with leaseAdmission (06-05A) and added the CLI test's binding mock (06-05B). MRC-06-08 (672) and MRC-06-09 (500) are test tasks whose lines are the tests, the shared 151-line test double and a 13-line product repair the Codex tests found. Every other task is inside the guideline and names one to three authored files; each continuation is recorded beside its task in MAESTRO-MEGA-06.md.

failedAttemptsPreserved: First run after MRC-06-01: 99 of the process handler tests failed with `processManager.spawnAdmitted is not a function`; the handler now spawns through the admitted path and the test's manager mock had only `spawn`. The mock learned `admitSpawn` (standalone), `spawnAdmitted` (delegating to `spawn`) and `terminalTabConfig`; no assertion changed (06-01B).

After MRC-06-03: `codexRouting` asserted the app-server spawner's options equal `{ clientVersion }` exactly; the options now carry the live `effects` read. The assertion was widened and checks the read answers null without a port (06-03B).

After MRC-06-05: 5 of the CLI spawner's #1608 cold-cache tests failed with the spawn never called. The new binding-file read ran under that suite's blanket `fs` mock (`existsSync` left true by an earlier test, `readFileSync` answering nothing), which reads as a corrupt enrollment and correctly fails closed; the suite now mocks `readManagedBindingFile` as absent (06-05B). Product behavior unchanged.

MRC-06-08's pending-revocation case found a real defect: a revoked pending Codex approval was answered through a placeholder method (`revoked`), which the answer table turns into a JSON-RPC method-not-found error instead of the method's own decline. The spawner now keeps the original request in its pending map and declines it by its method (06-08B, +13 -8 in CodexAppServerSpawner.ts).

MRC-06-09's first terminal-sink draft had a standalone `runCommand` case; the terminal attach suite mocks Windows, where the local runner spawns a real shell child. The case was dropped (the standalone runner is covered by LocalCommandRunner.test.ts) rather than spawn a shell in a unit test.
MRC-06-09's standalone CLI case first drove Codex with a `task_started` line only, which the shared resolver reads as no final text (a failure); it now emits an agent message.

Two Edit attempts on text the st-filtered file view had elided (relay server comments, the dispatch harness tail) did not match; the exact lines were read with /usr/bin/sed and patched with node scripts. The machine's Bash hook refused one inline command containing a non-ASCII character as 'control characters'; rerun with ASCII. The hook also blocks `rm` and `mv`, which is why the scratch test named under scratch is still in the tree.

deterministicCoverage.doubles: src/__tests__/helpers/managedSpawnPort.ts: fakeSpawnPort (the REAL createLocalHostAuthority and createContextVerifier over a policy table), tableEffects (an effect authority answering from a table or a pending promise), fakeAdmission (a plain admission object, refused as forged at the manager's sink). The Codex app-server is the suite's existing fake server; the relay client is a real socket.
cases: ProcessManager sink: no admission refused before any branch; look-alike admission forged; exact request admitted, changed prompt refused on digest; lease bound to the serve transport, spent on reuse, released on exit; policy denial as a decision; web-login actor the verifier refuses, authority never asked; revocation kills; spawner failure releases; standalone never asks

OpenCode: server key per authority/actor/policy apart from standalone; ask-mode config for a managed scope; route unavailable while unqualified; scope from the admission; permission events to exact effects
Codex routing: managed app-server turn without admission routes nothing; admission rides on the spawner config; live effects read answers the port

Codex app-server: positive accept bound to lease/thread/turn/request with the exact command effect; deny, unavailable and unknown decline under full-access args; no authority declines; pending request stays unanswered and is declined on Stop with the abort seen; exec fallback refused under management, kept standalone; pure effect extraction and codexRequestGranted

CLI: denied launch zero-effect and never retried as an effort rejection; enrolled machine without host unavailable; forged actor refused before the authority, forged lease refused at the spawn; effort retry under its own fresh admission with distinct request ids and snapshots; standalone binding unchanged

Terminal sinks: managed terminal tab refused without admission and PTY unavailable with one (lease released); preexisting terminal takes no input once managed, reason in the pane; local and SSH one-off commands refused at the runner with 126

Relay: managed deny answers the bridge without asking the user; user deny kept after a managed allow; user allow denied once the admission ended; allow+allow+live passes; throwing gate refuses, standalone gate leaves the user alone; the composed gate over fake process-manager deps denies without a live admission, decides the exact tool with the lease/actor/tab/request binding, answers not managed when standalone

protected-effects.outcomeRequired: Actual safe provider/tool child/file effect and denied child/egress through real endpoint/broker
protected-effects.state: Unchanged from 04 and 05: the Maestro side is built and exercised with the decision from a declared double; through the real endpoint the exchange still ends unauthenticated (no enrollment). Not passed; not counted.

sdk-effects-decided.outcomeRequired: A real Codex or OpenCode tool effect allowed and another denied through a real effect authority
sdk-effects-decided.state: The sinks decide every effect from the effect authority with the exact effect and binding, proven against the fake app-server and a table authority (allow accepted, deny/unavailable/unknown declined, pending revoked). No real provider ran and no real effect producer exists (the endpoint has no per-effect operation: CP-01, CP-03). Not passed; mock-only is not counted.

terminal-sinks-governed.outcomeRequired: A terminal or one-off command run through a qualified broker, or refused at the real sink with nothing started
terminal-sinks-governed.state: The refusal half is real and observed at the sinks (PTY unavailable, runner exit 126 with nothing spawned, input blocked); the qualified-broker half has no producer. A denial-only route is not a working feature and is not counted as positive.

cli-admission.outcomeRequired: A CLI launch admitted and one denied through the real endpoint authority with zero effect on denial
cli-admission.state: Admission on every spawn with zero effect on denial is proven over the real lease authority and a policy table; the real endpoint authority is not reachable (CP-01, CP-02). Not passed.
